name: Stans
kurzbeschreibung: Historic village at the entrance to the Zillertal, home to the oldest Zillertaler farmhouse and the parish church.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Stans is located in the Tyrolean Lower Inntal valley in the district of Schwaz at an elevation of 563 metres above sea level on the northern bank of the River Inn, directly beneath the forested slopes of the Karwendel Nature Park and the striking Stanser Joch (2,102 m). Situated approximately thirty kilometres east of Innsbruck within the Silberregion Karwendel, this traditional municipality has around 2,200 residents. Stans is famed for its captivating blend of pristine alpine nature and profound cultural history: the village serves as the gateway to the renowned Wolfsklamm gorge, to the clifftop pilgrimage monastery of St. Georgenberg (Tyrol's oldest pilgrimage site), and to the Renaissance gem Schloss Tratzberg. Lined with handsome Tyrolean farmhouses, two architecturally notable churches, and mixed alpine woodlands, Stans offers an unforgettable blend of natural spectacle, outdoor adventure, and historical heritage.

Geschichte

Stans ranks among the earliest documented settlements in Tyrol: it was recorded as early as 827 AD in the historic 'Quartinus Deed'—a land endowment from nobleman Quartinus to the monastery of Innichen—under the name 'Stauanes'. Over millennia, the Stanser Bach torrent carved a dramatic chasm through the Karwendel limestone; in 1901, this natural gorge was opened to the public as the 'Wolfsklamm' with wooden footbridges, stairways, and galleries. High above the gorge perches St. Georgenberg: founded around 950 AD as a hermitage by Blessed Rathold of Aibling, it became a Benedictine abbey in 1138 and Tyrol's premier pilgrimage destination following the Eucharistic Miracle of 1310. An engineering triumph is the Hohe Brücke built in 1497, Tyrol's oldest surviving timber bridge, spanning the gorge on a 40-metre-tall stone pillar. Overlooking the valley, Schloss Tratzberg was built around 1500 by the Tänzel brothers and expanded after 1554 by the Augsburg Fugger family into a lavish Renaissance palace. In the village, the neo-Gothic Sacred Heart church (1884–1896) and the late Gothic St. Lawrence church illustrate deep-seated spiritual roots.

Anreise

By car, Stans is reached via the Inntal motorway A12 using either the Schwaz exit (Exit 43) or the Vomp exit, continuing along the federal highway B171 into the village within minutes. Ample visitor parking is provided at the entrance to Wolfsklamm gorge and at the foot of Schloss Tratzberg. Train passengers take the Lower Inntal railway line to Stans bei Schwaz station, served at frequent intervals by S-Bahn Tirol trains (lines S4 and S5 from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, Kufstein, and Wörgl; journey time from Innsbruck roughly 25 minutes). Regional VVT buses link Stans with the train hubs at Schwaz and Jenbach. Cyclists can access the village directly from the long-distance Innradweg R3 cycle route.

Tipps

A walk through the Wolfsklamm gorge is an essential highlight: 354 wooden stairs, catwalks, and cliff-hewn paths lead past thundering waterfalls and turquoise pools through the rugged gorge (open from May to early November). At the top, cross the remarkable Hohe Brücke from 1497 to reach the clifftop sanctuary of St. Georgenberg, complete with its pilgrimage church and rustic pilgrim inn. For a rewarding loop, continue along the forest path to Schloss Tratzberg: this fully furnished Renaissance castle features the 46-metre-long Habsburg Hall, historic armouries, and state-of-the-art virtual reality tours. The Tratzberg-Express slow train runs between the valley and the castle gates. In the village centre, take time to visit the twin heritage churches of St. Laurentius and Herz Jesu.
